meta.actor: Claude — consolidation pass (no research, no content rewriting)
meta.scope: Every Grok batch file for BRICS international layer merged into one file. Records are byte-faithful to the batches except for the normalisations listed in _consolidation.

reports.title: New Development Bank Environment and Social Framework (ESF)
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Core operational policy document of the New Development Bank setting out the Bank’s approach to environmental and social risk management. Contains Part 1 (Environment and Social Policy) and Part 2 (Environmental and Social Standards covering assessment, involuntary resettlement, and indigenous peoples). Applies to all NDB-financed or administered projects. Version dated March 2016 (V4). Continuously referenced in project documents, Annual Reports, and evaluation work as the governing E&S standard.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the New Development Bank and the Members of the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and Members of the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
reports.description: MoU signed 22 June 2022 establishing a framework for cooperation between the NDB and the national development / export-import banks that constitute the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism. Covers co-financing, knowledge sharing, local-currency instruments, and project pipeline development. Builds on earlier interbank cooperation arrangements among the founding members’ development banks.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the New Development Bank and the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center (BPIC)
reports.description: MoU establishing a framework for strategic, technical and operational cooperation between NDB and the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center (a public institution under Fujian Provincial Government, outcome of the 13th BRICS Summit). Focus areas include new industrial revolution technologies, artificial intelligence, trade, investment and people-to-people exchanges. Signed text publicly available.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding on Strategic Cooperation between the New Development Bank and the BRICS Business Council
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and BRICS Business Council
reports.description: MoU signed 4 September 2017 in Xiamen during the 9th BRICS Summit in the presence of BRICS Leaders. Establishes a framework for long-term cooperation including facilitation of project sponsorship, exploration of local-currency use in NDB funding, knowledge exchange, and joint research on priority issues facing BRICS countries from the business-sector perspective.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the New Development Bank and the BRICS Export Credit Agencies
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and BRICS Export Credit Agencies (ABGF, EXIAR, ECGC, SINOSURE, ECIC)
reports.description: MoU signed 13 June 2017 between NDB and the five founding members’ export credit / investment insurance agencies, including Russia’s EXIAR (Russian Agency for Export Credit and Investment Insurance). Purpose is to develop cooperation on guarantees and insurance for NDB-financed and co-financed projects, knowledge sharing on risk evaluation and insurance, and capacity building.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the New Development Bank and JSC Russian Railways
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and JSC Russian Railways
reports.description: MoU signed 6 September 2017 on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok. Establishes a framework for general cooperation on infrastructure projects, particularly high-speed railways, public-private partnership opportunities, and knowledge sharing. Explicitly references potential development of the Moscow–Kazan high-speed railway among other projects in NDB member countries.

reports.title: Joint Statement by the Heads of BRICS National Statistical Offices (Fortaleza, 11–12 June 2025)
reports.publisher: Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS (Brazilian host)
reports.description: Joint Statement issued at the Summit of the Heads of BRICS National Statistical Offices held in Fortaleza, Brazil, 11–12 June 2025. Records decisions on the Joint Statistical Publication work programme, support for a Workshop on Indicators for the Digital Age, creation of an Observatory on National Experiences in Economic Development, Poverty Reduction and Climate Change Mitigation, proposal for an International Training Centre, endorsement of a BRICS Statistical Journal, and congratulations on the JSP Snapshot. Attended by delegations from confirmed full members including Russia (Rosstat).

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the World Bank Group and the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: World Bank Group (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA) and New Development Bank
reports.description: MoU setting out mutual cooperation between the World Bank Group and NDB in areas including co-financing of projects, knowledge exchange, advisory services, human-resources secondments, treasury management, and training. Explicitly situates NDB’s mandate under the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank. One of the earliest formal partnership instruments signed by NDB with a major multilateral development bank group.

reports.title: Framework Agreement on Financial Cooperation within the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
reports.publisher: Development banks of the BRICS founding members (BNDES, VEB/VEB.RF, Exim Bank of India, China Development Bank, DBSA)
reports.description: Foundational interbank framework signed in 2011 by the national development banks of the original BRICS members. Establishes the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism for strengthening financial cooperation, facilitating trade and investment, and promoting local-currency credit lines and knowledge sharing. Later revised to accommodate new members. Serves as the institutional precursor referenced by subsequent NDB–ICM MoUs.

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding between the Islamic Development Bank Group and the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: Islamic Development Bank Group and New Development Bank
reports.description: MoU signed 10 December 2025 in Jeddah establishing a framework for strategic partnership on infrastructure and sustainable development. Covers joint operations, co-financing, technical cooperation, knowledge-sharing, renewable energy, transport, water and sanitation, climate finance, and private capital mobilisation. Explicit South-South cooperation framing.

reports.title: VII BRICS Summit Ufa Declaration (9 July 2015)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the VII BRICS Summit in Ufa, Russian Federation. Explicitly welcomes the entry into force of the Agreement on the New Development Bank and the Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement, the inaugural meeting of the NDB Board of Governors, and the signing of the Inter-Central Bank Agreement under the CRA. Records the operationalisation of both institutions as major outcomes of the Fortaleza instruments.

reports.title: VIII BRICS Summit Goa Declaration (16 October 2016)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the VIII BRICS Summit in Goa, India. Notes with satisfaction the operationalisation of the New Development Bank and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement, welcomes the first set of NDB loans (particularly renewable-energy projects), the issuance of the first RMB green bonds by NDB, and progress on the Africa Regional Centre. Reaffirms the institutions created in 2014 as contributions to the global financial architecture.

reports.title: XIV BRICS Summit Beijing Declaration (23 June 2022)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XIV BRICS Summit in Beijing. Congratulates NDB on relocation to its permanent headquarters in Shanghai and the opening of the Indian Regional Office. Welcomes decisions on admission of four new members to the NDB and looks forward to further gradual and balanced expansion. Supports amendments to the CRA Treaty and related documents to enhance flexibility and responsiveness; notes progress on CRA test runs and coordination with the IMF.

reports.title: XVII BRICS Summit Rio de Janeiro Declaration (2025)
reports.publisher: Leaders of BRICS countries (Brazilian presidency)
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XVII BRICS Summit held in Rio de Janeiro under Brazilian chairmanship (2025). Continues the series of summit political instruments that reaffirm support for the New Development Bank, Contingent Reserve Arrangement, and broader BRICS economic-financial architecture. Issued under the theme of strengthening Global South cooperation.

reports.title: New Development Bank Official Members List (Founding and New Members)
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Authoritative public listing maintained by the New Development Bank of its founding members (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa — all effective 3 July 2015) and subsequent new members with effective dates: Bangladesh (16 Sept 2021), United Arab Emirates (4 Oct 2021), Egypt (20 Feb 2023), Algeria (19 May 2025), Uzbekistan (5 June 2026). Prospective members (admitted by Board of Governors but awaiting deposit of instrument of accession) are also recorded. Constitutes the official record of membership status under the 2014 Agreement and the 2017 Terms for Admission of New Members.

reports.title: Egypt Instrument of Accession / Formal Membership in the New Development Bank (effective 20 February 2023)
reports.publisher: Government of the Arab Republic of Egypt and New Development Bank
reports.description: Formal accession of Egypt to the New Development Bank. Egypt was admitted by the NDB Board of Governors; membership became effective upon completion of domestic procedures and deposit of the instrument of accession on 20 February 2023. Documented in official NDB announcements and the Bank’s members list. Links Egypt (a 2024 BRICS full member) into the NDB capital and governance structure created by the 2014 Agreement.

reports.title: United Arab Emirates Formal Membership in the New Development Bank (effective 4 October 2021)
reports.publisher: Government of the United Arab Emirates and New Development Bank
reports.region: United Arab Emirates / BRICS / NDB members
reports.description: Formal accession of the United Arab Emirates to the New Development Bank. UAE was among the first non-founding members admitted in the 2021 expansion round; membership became effective 4 October 2021 upon deposit of the instrument of accession. Recorded in the official NDB members list and contemporary announcements. Links a 2024 BRICS full member into the NDB structure.

reports.title: Interbank Local Currency Credit Line Agreement (Master Agreement) under the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
reports.publisher: Development banks of the BRICS founding members (BNDES, VEB.RF / Vnesheconombank, Exim Bank of India, China Development Bank, DBSA)
reports.description: Master / framework agreement establishing guidelines for the extension of credit facilities in local currencies among the national development banks participating in the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism. Original version associated with the 2011–2012 ICM framework; subsequent revisions (including a 2024 revision to accommodate new members) have been signed. Intended to reduce exchange-rate risk and support intra-BRICS trade and investment. Operationalisation has remained limited (few bilateral credit lines activated).

reports.title: Multilateral Letter of Credit Confirmation Facility Agreement under the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism
reports.publisher: Development banks of the BRICS founding members (BNDES, VEB.RF, Exim Bank of India, China Development Bank, DBSA)
reports.description: Companion agreement to the Local Currency Credit Line Master Agreement, defining rules for letters of credit in export operations among the five founding members’ development banks. Signed in the early operational phase of the ICM (circa 2012) and referenced in subsequent ICM documentation. Forms part of the practical interbank toolkit intended to facilitate trade settlement outside traditional dollar channels.

reports.title: Algeria Formal Membership in the New Development Bank (effective 19 May 2025)
reports.publisher: Government of the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria and New Development Bank
reports.description: Formal accession of Algeria to the New Development Bank. Algeria deposited its instrument of accession on 19 May 2025, becoming a full member. Documented in official NDB announcements. While Algeria is not a full BRICS member, its NDB membership expands the Bank’s African and Mediterranean reach under the same 2014 constitutive framework.

reports.title: IX BRICS Summit Xiamen Declaration (4 September 2017)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the IX BRICS Summit in Xiamen, China. Records satisfaction with results of cooperation including the establishment of the New Development Bank and Contingent Reserve Arrangement. Welcomes the launch of the NDB Africa Regional Centre, the setting-up of the Project Preparation Fund, approval of the second batch of projects, and ground-breaking of the permanent headquarters building.

reports.title: 10th BRICS Summit Johannesburg Declaration (27 July 2018)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the 10th BRICS Summit in Johannesburg, South Africa. Notes steps to strengthen operational readiness of the CRA and welcomes a successful test run of the de-linked portion. Welcomes the upcoming establishment of the Americas Regional Office in São Paulo and notes NDB Board of Governors discussions on innovative approaches for development finance.

reports.title: XI BRICS Summit Brasília Declaration (14 November 2019)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XI BRICS Summit in Brasília. Notes with appreciation the role of the NDB in infrastructure and sustainable development financing and marks the 5th anniversary of the signing of the NDB Articles of Agreement in Fortaleza. Welcomes the establishment of the Americas Regional Office in São Paulo (with sub-office in Brasília) and looks forward to the opening of the remaining regional offices in Russia and India. Notes further CRA preparedness steps and a second test run.

reports.title: XII BRICS Summit Moscow Declaration (17 November 2020)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XII BRICS Summit (held by video conference under Russian chairmanship). Commends the NDB for COVID-19 emergency assistance (up to USD 10 billion Emergency Assistance Program). Welcomes the opening of the NDB Eurasian Regional Centre in Moscow and looks forward to the Indian regional office. Supports the NDB membership-expansion process and notes progress on amendments to CRA documents.

reports.title: XIII BRICS Summit New Delhi Declaration (9 September 2021)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XIII BRICS Summit under Indian chairmanship. Recognises the creation of the NDB and CRA among the major achievements of 15 years of BRICS cooperation. Looks forward to the Bank’s second General Strategy for 2022–26, encourages financing of social infrastructure and digital projects, and urges greater mobilisation of private capital and co-financing. Welcomes the successful completion of the fourth CRA test run and supports improved CRA–IMF coordination.

reports.title: Decreto nº 8.624 of 29 December 2015 — Promulgation of the Agreement on the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: Presidency of the Federative Republic of Brazil
reports.description: Brazilian domestic promulgation instrument for the Agreement on the New Development Bank signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014. Notes that the National Congress approved the Agreement by Decreto Legislativo nº 131 of 3 June 2015 and that the Agreement entered into force for Brazil on 3 July 2015. Completes the domestic legal steps required for Brazil’s participation as a founding member.

reports.title: New Development Bank Special Appropriation Bill / Act 2015 (South Africa)
reports.publisher: Parliament of the Republic of South Africa / National Treasury
reports.description: South African legislative instrument appropriating funds for the first capital instalment to the New Development Bank and confirming parliamentary ratification of the 2014 Agreement. Records that South Africa ratified the Agreement through Parliament on 18 June 2015 and that the Agreement entered into force for all BRICS countries on 3 July 2015. Provides the domestic legal and budgetary basis for South Africa’s founding-member capital contribution.

reports.title: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress Ratification of the Agreement on the New Development Bank (1 July 2015)
reports.publisher: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of the People’s Republic of China
reports.description: Chinese domestic ratification of the Agreement on the New Development Bank. The Standing Committee of the NPC approved the Agreement on 1 July 2015, enabling China to deposit its instrument of acceptance/ratification and contributing to the Agreement’s entry into force on 3 July 2015. Documented in contemporary official and state-media reports.

reports.title: New Development Bank Procurement Policy
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Core operational policy document governing procurement of goods, works and services financed by the New Development Bank. Version dated March 2016 (V4). Explicitly grounded in Article 21 of the Agreement on the New Development Bank. Sets out principles of economy, efficiency, fairness, transparency, quality and value for money, and applies to all NDB-financed projects.

reports.title: Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership (adopted at the Ufa Summit, 2015)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Medium-term strategic framework for expanding trade, investment, manufacturing, financial cooperation, connectivity and ICT cooperation among the BRICS countries. Adopted at the VII BRICS Summit in Ufa (2015) and referenced in subsequent Leaders’ Declarations as a key guideline for economic partnership. Complements the institutional architecture of the NDB and CRA.

reports.title: New Development Bank Information Disclosure Policy
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Core governance policy setting out NDB’s approach to transparency and public access to information. Explicitly grounded in Article 15 of the Articles of Agreement (transparency of proceedings and access to documents). Establishes the presumption of disclosure, principles of transparency and accountability, and categories of confidential information. Version 2017 V2 (June 2017).

reports.title: New Development Bank Anti-Corruption, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money Laundering Policy
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Core integrity policy providing the conceptual framework for prohibited practices (corruption, fraud, collusion, coercion, obstructive practices, money laundering). Sets zero-tolerance approach, investigation procedures, and responsibilities of Bank personnel and counterparties. Originally approved 12 April 2016; subsequent revisions documented. Applies across all NDB operations and projects in member countries.

reports.title: New Development Bank Code of Business Conduct and Ethics
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Internal ethical framework for Bank personnel covering integrity, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and use of information. Cross-references the Information Disclosure Policy and the Anti-Corruption Policy. Multiple revised versions exist (including 2021 and 2024); treated here as the living titled instrument governing staff conduct.

reports.title: New Development Bank Whistleblower Procedures
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Procedural instrument protecting individuals who report misconduct or wrongdoing in good faith. Grounded in the Anti-Corruption Policy and the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics. Sets out reporting channels, confidentiality protections, and investigation handling by the Compliance and Investigations Department.

reports.title: BRICS Business Council Annual Report
reports.publisher: BRICS Business Council (rotating national chapter / presidency)
reports.description: Recurring annual report presented by the BRICS Business Council to BRICS Leaders. Contains strategic recommendations, policy actions, and private-sector initiatives across working groups (infrastructure, agribusiness, energy, finance, skills, etc.). Explicitly and repeatedly calls for cooperation with the New Development Bank, including dedicated financing lines, fast-track processes for low-carbon projects, and infrastructure funds. 2025 edition (Brazilian presidency) and prior editions (including 2023/24 Russian presidency) are publicly available.

reports.title: BRICS Business Council Annual Report 2025 — Business Cooperation for an Inclusive and Sustainable Future
reports.publisher: BRICS Business Council (Brazilian presidency)
reports.description: 2025 edition of the BRICS Business Council Annual Report, prepared under Brazilian chairmanship and presented in Rio de Janeiro. Contains high-level recommendations, policy actions, and 47 private-sector initiatives. Explicitly recommends creation of a fund for private companies in the infrastructure sector within the New Development Bank and a fast-track process for low-carbon emission projects to obtain NDB financing. Reflects the expanded membership (including Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Iran).

reports.title: Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the Fields of Science, Technology and Innovation among the Governments of the BRICS States (2015)
reports.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Intergovernmental MoU establishing a strategic framework for cooperation in science, technology and innovation among the five founding BRICS members. Signed / approved around the Ufa period (Russian Government order of 14 March 2015 refers to the draft). Forms part of the broader BRICS institutional architecture that later produced the Partnership on New Industrial Revolution and related innovation-centre instruments.

reports.title: New Development Bank Evaluation Policy
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Policy governing independent evaluation of NDB operations and results. Approved by the Board of Directors (2022, with subsequent revision in 2024). Provides the methodological and institutional basis for the work of the Independent Evaluation Office, including the Development Results reports that assess alignment with NDB strategies and member-country priorities.

reports.title: Technical Meetings of the National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries (preparatory process for the Joint Statistical Publication)
reports.publisher: National Statistical Offices of BRICS (rotating host)
reports.description: Recurring technical-level meetings of experts from BRICS NSOs dedicated to the preparation of each year’s Joint Statistical Publication and Snapshot. Held under the chairmanship of the host NSO; sets data requirements, chapter structure, timelines, and methodological harmonisation. Documented in Rosstat and other NSO announcements as a standing cooperation mechanism that underpins the annual JSP series.

reports.title: BRICS Joint Statistical Publication 2024
reports.publisher: National Statistical Offices of BRICS (Rosstat host for 2024 edition)
reports.description: 2024 edition of the annual BRICS Joint Statistical Publication, compiled under Russian chairmanship (Rosstat). Contains comparable socio-economic statistics contributed by the NSOs of the full members. Presented in conjunction with the Kazan Summit and accompanied by an online BI platform. Forms part of the continuous JSP series that began in 2010.

reports.title: Amended Rules of Procedure of the Board of Governors of the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Rules of Procedure of the Board of Governors, adopted at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Governors on 7 July 2015 and amended on 20 July 2016. Explicitly complementary to the Agreement on the New Development Bank and its Articles of Agreement; in case of conflict the Agreement and Articles prevail. Governs annual and special meetings, chairpersonship, voting (including qualified and special majorities), and related procedures of the highest decision-making body.

reports.title: Amended Rules of Procedure of the Board of Directors of the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Rules of Procedure of the Board of Directors, adopted at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Governors on 7 July 2015 and amended by the Board of Governors on 20 July 2016. Complementary to the 2014 Agreement and Articles of Agreement. Governs the non-resident Board’s conduct of general operations, chairpersonship, committees, and decision-making.

reports.title: New Development Bank Board of Directors Governance Structure
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Document setting out the governance structure of the Board of Directors, including committees (Audit, Risk and Compliance; Budget, Human Resources and Compensation). Originally approved January 2016 with subsequent amendments. Locates the Board’s responsibilities under the Articles of Agreement and describes the committee architecture that supports Board decision-making.

reports.title: New Development Bank Policy on Sovereign Loans and Loans with Sovereign Guarantee
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Operational policy covering NDB sovereign loans and loans with sovereign guarantee to member countries, as allowed under Articles 18 and 19 of the Agreement on the New Development Bank. Sets eligibility, pricing elements (front-end fee, commitment charge), processing steps, and change-control rules. Multiple amended versions exist (2016 original, later revisions including 2019 and 2024 processing variants).

reports.title: New Development Bank Policy on Financial Management and Financial Analysis, and Economic Analysis of Projects
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Policy requiring that NDB-financed projects are governed by sound financial management arrangements, are financially viable, and produce equitable and sustainable economic benefits. Explicitly grounded in Article 21 (sound banking principles, economy and efficiency) and Article 13e (decisions based only on economic considerations) of the Articles of Agreement. Originally approved 21 January 2016; later versions exist.

reports.title: New Development Bank Policy on Loans to International Organisations
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Policy governing NDB loans to international organisations, grounded in Article 1 of the Articles of Agreement (cooperation with international organisations and other financial entities). Sets juridical-personality, immunity-waiver, exposure-limit and assessment requirements. Approved 12 September 2019.

reports.title: BRICS Action Plan for Innovation Cooperation (2017–2020)
reports.publisher: BRICS countries (Science, Technology and Innovation track)
reports.description: Action Plan adopted under the BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation cooperation framework. Builds on the 2015 MoU on STI Cooperation. Sets concrete steps for exchanges of good practices, networks of science parks and incubators, cross-cultural talent pools, and related deliverables for the period 2017–2020. Implemented through the BRICS STIEP Working Group.

reports.title: BRICS Trade in Services Cooperation Roadmap (2017)
reports.publisher: BRICS Contact Group on Economic and Trade Issues / Trade Ministers
reports.description: Roadmap endorsed by BRICS Trade Ministers in 2017 under the Chinese presidency. Builds on the 2015 Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership (which identified services as a priority) and the 2016 Framework for Cooperation on Trade in Services. Identifies areas for cooperation including tourism, health, audiovisual, professional, computer, R&D, telecommunication and financial services.

reports.title: BRICS Implementation Roadmap on Trade and Investment related aspects of the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2025 (2021)
reports.publisher: BRICS Contact Group on Economic and Trade Issues (Indian presidency context)
reports.description: Implementation Roadmap endorsed in 2021 for the trade and investment components of the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2025. Covers investment facilitation, trade in services, customs cooperation, intellectual-property cooperation, MSMEs, and related actions. References earlier frameworks including the Outlines for BRICS Investment Facilitation and the Trade in Services Roadmap.

reports.title: Joint Statement of the BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (11 October 2024)
reports.publisher: BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (Russian chairmanship)
reports.description: Joint Statement issued under Russia’s 2024 chairmanship ahead of the Kazan Summit. Addresses local currencies, payment instruments and platforms; welcomes the conceptual document on the BRICS Cross-Border Payments Initiative (BCBPI); notes work on settlements in national currencies, correspondent banking, and the BRICS Payment Task Force. Also references NDB development and the BRICS Think Tank Network for Finance.

reports.title: Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2025
reports.publisher: Leaders / BRICS countries (prepared under Russian presidency 2020, endorsed subsequently)
reports.description: Updated medium-term strategy succeeding the 2015 Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership. Encompasses trade, investment, manufacturing, financial cooperation, connectivity, digital economy and related pillars. Implementation roadmaps for trade and investment aspects were developed under subsequent presidencies. Referenced in Leaders’ Declarations and ministerial documents from 2020–2021 onward.

reports.title: Joint Statement of the Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries (Lucknow, August 2026)
reports.publisher: Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS (Indian host)
reports.description: Joint Statement adopted at the meeting of Heads of NSOs held in Lucknow under India’s 2026 BRICS presidency. Reaffirms commitment to deepen cooperation on official statistics, digital dissemination, administrative data, artificial intelligence, reforms of national statistical systems, and coordinated transition to the System of National Accounts 2025. Continues the annual Heads of NSOs series that governs the Joint Statistical Publication work programme.

reports.title: BRICS Joint Statistical Publication Snapshot 2025
reports.publisher: National Statistical Offices of BRICS (rotating host)
reports.description: 2025 edition of the shorter companion Snapshot to the full BRICS Joint Statistical Publication. Contains selected key comparable indicators drawn from the main JSP for wider dissemination. Continues the annual Snapshot series launched in 2021.

reports.title: New Development Bank Technical Assistance Policy
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Policy governing technical assistance provided by the New Development Bank. Listed among core Board-approved operational policies; amended as of May 2022. Supports project preparation, capacity building and knowledge services consistent with the Bank’s mandate under the 2014 Agreement.

reports.title: New Development Bank Policy on Guarantees
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Policy governing the use of guarantees by the New Development Bank. Amended as of June 2019. Forms part of the suite of financial-instrument policies that operationalise the Bank’s ability to support projects through loans, guarantees, equity participation and other instruments under the Articles of Agreement.

reports.title: Strategic Framework of BRICS Customs Cooperation (2017)
reports.publisher: BRICS Customs administrations / Trade track
reports.description: Strategic Framework signed in 2017 specifying cooperation among BRICS customs administrations, including experience sharing on the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, authorised economic operators, compatibility of national single-window mechanisms, and related trade-facilitation measures. Referenced in subsequent Implementation Roadmaps and Trade Ministers’ outcomes.

reports.title: BRICS Joint Statistical Publication (JSP)
reports.publisher: National Statistical Offices of BRICS (rotating host; Rosstat 2024, IBGE 2025)
reports.description: Annual joint compilation of comparable socio-economic statistics (population, labour force, national accounts, price indices, living standards, industry, energy, external relations, etc.) produced by the national statistical offices of the BRICS full members. First issued 2010; continuous annual series. Presented at BRICS summits. 2024 edition compiled under Russian chairmanship; 2025 under Brazilian. Includes summary comparison tables and country-specific tables. From 2021 a shorter Snapshot companion is also issued. 2024 also launched an online BI platform based on the historical series.

reports.title: BRICS Joint Statistical Publication Snapshot
reports.publisher: National Statistical Offices of BRICS (rotating host)
reports.description: Shorter companion version of the full BRICS Joint Statistical Publication, issued annually since 2021 for wider user engagement. Contains selected key comparable indicators drawn from the full JSP.

reports.title: Agreement on the New Development Bank (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014) and annexed Articles of Agreement
reports.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People's Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Foundational treaty establishing the New Development Bank (NDB). Signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014 by the five founding BRICS members. Entered into force 3 July 2015 after all five deposited instruments of acceptance/ratification. Russia ratified by Federal Law No. 29-FZ of 8 March 2015. Creates the Bank, sets purpose (mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development in BRICS and other EMDCs), capital structure (initial authorised USD 100 bn, subscribed USD 50 bn), governance, and membership rules. Continuously cited as the legal basis in every subsequent NDB Annual Report, strategy document, and project approval.

reports.title: Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014)
reports.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People's Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: International treaty establishing a self-managed Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) of USD 100 billion among the five founding BRICS members. Signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014. Purpose: provide liquidity and precautionary instruments in response to actual or potential short-term balance-of-payments pressures; complement the global financial safety net (IMF, bilateral swaps, own reserves). Individual commitments: China USD 41 bn; Brazil, India, Russia USD 18 bn each; South Africa USD 5 bn. Entered into force after all parties completed domestic procedures (announced at 7th BRICS Summit 2015). Resources remain with national central banks until drawn via currency swap.

reports.title: New Development Bank Annual Report
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Recurring official annual report of the New Development Bank covering operational results (project approvals, portfolio), financial statements, strategy progress, membership, and governance. Explicitly references the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank as the constitutive instrument. 2024 edition (published Dec 2025) reports 15 new loans totalling USD 4.5 bn, cumulative approvals ~USD 39 bn, net portfolio USD 35.2 bn. Includes country-level project examples (including Russia).

reports.title: NDB General Strategy 2022–2026
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Medium-term strategic framework of the New Development Bank for the period 2022–2026. Sets operational priorities, membership expansion approach, climate and sustainability focus, and capital utilisation goals. Builds directly on the 2014 Agreement and the preceding 2017–2021 strategy. Cited in subsequent Annual Reports as the governing strategy cycle.

reports.title: NDB General Strategy 2017–2021
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: First five-year general strategy of the New Development Bank covering 2017–2021. Laid out the initial operational approach, project priorities, and membership expansion path after the Bank’s establishment under the 2014 Agreement. Succeeded by the 2022–2026 Strategy. Cited in later Annual Reports and strategy documents as the foundational strategy cycle.

reports.title: Joint Statement by the Heads of BRICS National Statistical Offices
reports.publisher: Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS (rotating host)
reports.description: Annual joint statement issued at the Summit / Meeting of the Heads of BRICS National Statistical Offices. Records decisions on the Joint Statistical Publication work programme, data harmonisation, new initiatives (e.g. Statistical Journal, Observatory proposals, digital-age indicators), and host arrangements for the following year. Rosstat regularly participates; Russia has hosted. 2025 Fortaleza statement (Brazil host) lists attending delegations from confirmed full members.

reports.title: Agreement between the Government of the Russian Federation and the New Development Bank on Hosting the New Development Bank Eurasian Regional Centre in the Russian Federation
reports.publisher: Government of the Russian Federation and New Development Bank
reports.description: Host-country agreement signed in Brasília on 13 November 2019 during the 11th BRICS Summit. Provides for the establishment and operation of the NDB Eurasian Regional Centre (ERC) in Moscow. Grants the Centre legal personality, immunities and privileges analogous to other international organisations in Russia, tax exemptions for official activities, and facilities support from the Russian Government. Ratified by Russia via Federal Law No. 359-FZ of 9 November 2020; entered into force 7 December 2020. Explicitly references the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank and its Articles of Agreement as the basis for the Centre’s existence.

reports.title: Federal Law No. 359-FZ of 9 November 2020 on Ratification of the Agreement between the Government of the Russian Federation and the New Development Bank on Hosting the New Development Bank Eurasian Regional Centre in the Russian Federation
reports.publisher: Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation / President of the Russian Federation
reports.description: Russian domestic ratification instrument for the 2019 NDB Eurasian Regional Centre host agreement. Signed by President Putin on 9 November 2020. Completes the domestic legal steps required for the host agreement to enter into force (7 December 2020). Serves as the formal Russian legal act that brings the international host agreement into effect on Russian territory.

reports.title: Federal Law No. 29-FZ of 8 March 2015 on Ratification of the Agreement on the New Development Bank
reports.publisher: Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation / President of the Russian Federation
reports.description: Russian domestic ratification instrument for the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement on the New Development Bank (and its annexed Articles of Agreement). Completes the domestic legal steps that allowed Russia’s instrument of acceptance to be deposited, contributing to the Agreement’s entry into force on 3 July 2015.

reports.title: XVI BRICS Summit Kazan Declaration — Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security (23 October 2024)
reports.publisher: Leaders of BRICS countries (Russian Federation presidency)
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XVI BRICS Summit held in Kazan, Russian Federation, 22–24 October 2024 under the theme ‘Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security’. Reaffirms the three pillars of cooperation, welcomes expansion outcomes, and records decisions on economic-financial architecture, including continued support for the New Development Bank and related mechanisms. Issued under Russian chairmanship; serves as a high-level political instrument that recurringly references the institutional architecture established in 2014.

reports.title: Inter-Central Bank Agreement under the BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (implementing Article 6 of the 2014 CRA Treaty)
reports.publisher: Central Bank of Brazil, Central Bank of the Russian Federation, Reserve Bank of India, People’s Bank of China, South African Reserve Bank
reports.description: Operational agreement required by Article 6 of the Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014). Sets out the required operational procedures and guidelines for liquidity and precautionary instruments, including currency-swap mechanics among the five founding central banks. The Treaty itself mandates this inter-central-bank agreement as the vehicle for executing transactions. While the full operational text is not always publicly released in the same manner as the Treaty, its existence and function are explicitly required by the Treaty and referenced in subsequent CRA governance descriptions.

reports.title: Agreement between the New Development Bank and the Government of the People’s Republic of China Regarding the Headquarters of the New Development Bank in Shanghai, China
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and Government of the People’s Republic of China
reports.description: Host-country agreement establishing the permanent headquarters of the New Development Bank in Shanghai. Provides the legal framework for the Bank’s seat, privileges, immunities and operational facilities in China. Listed among NDB core HQ/Host Country Agreements; continuously referenced as the constitutive host instrument for headquarters operations.

reports.title: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of South Africa and the New Development Bank on the Hosting of the New Development Bank Africa Regional Centre in the Republic of South Africa
reports.publisher: Government of the Republic of South Africa and New Development Bank
reports.description: Host-country agreement signed 17 August 2017 and entered into force 25 October 2017. Establishes the first regional office of the NDB — the Africa Regional Centre (ARC) — in Johannesburg. Explicitly takes into account the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank and recalls Article 4 of the Articles of Agreement providing that the first regional office shall be in Johannesburg. Grants the Centre legal personality, immunities and privileges.

reports.title: Agreement between the New Development Bank and the Government of the Federative Republic of Brazil on the Hosting of the New Development Bank Americas Regional Office in the Federative Republic of Brazil
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and Government of the Federative Republic of Brazil
reports.description: Host-country agreement establishing the Americas Regional Office (ARO) with seat in São Paulo and a sub-office in Brasília. Signed 2018; operations commenced 2019. Completes the regional-office network for the Western Hemisphere under the powers of the 2014 Articles of Agreement.

reports.title: Agreement between the New Development Bank and the Government of the Republic of India on the Hosting of the New Development Bank Indian Regional Office in the Republic of India
reports.publisher: New Development Bank and Government of the Republic of India
reports.description: Host-country agreement establishing the Indian Regional Office (IRO) in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City). Finalised 2021; includes provision for sub-regional offices subject to operational needs and government approval. Completes the set of founding-member regional offices.

reports.title: Fortaleza Declaration (6th BRICS Summit, 15 July 2014)
reports.publisher: Leaders of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People’s Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the Sixth BRICS Summit in Fortaleza, Brazil, on 15 July 2014 under the theme ‘Inclusive Growth: Sustainable Solutions’. Announces the signing of the Agreement on the New Development Bank and the Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement. Records the initial capital of the NDB (authorised USD 100 bn, subscribed USD 50 bn) and the CRA (USD 100 bn). Serves as the high-level political instrument contemporaneous with the two foundational treaties.

reports.title: XV BRICS Summit Johannesburg II Declaration (23 August 2023)
reports.publisher: Leaders of BRICS countries (South African presidency)
reports.description: Leaders’ declaration adopted at the XV BRICS Summit in Sandton, Gauteng, South Africa, 22–24 August 2023. Records the decision on membership expansion (invitations to Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Argentina — the last of which later withdrew) and reaffirms support for the New Development Bank and Contingent Reserve Arrangement as pillars of the BRICS economic-financial architecture. Issued under South African chairmanship.

reports.title: Independent Evaluation Office Report on NDB’s Development Results (First Edition, with a Focus on Climate and Environment)
reports.publisher: Independent Evaluation Office of the New Development Bank
reports.description: First synthesis report of the NDB Independent Evaluation Office (IEO), consolidating findings from 13 independent evaluations conducted 2022–2024. Covers projects representing approximately 56% of NDB’s total disbursed financing by July 2024. Assesses relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability against national priorities, NDB general strategies and the SDGs. Explicitly references NDB General Strategies and project-level results frameworks. Published 2024/2025.

reports.title: Terms, Conditions and Procedures for the Admission of New Members (1 April 2017)
reports.publisher: New Development Bank
reports.description: Board-approved document setting out the formal terms, conditions and procedures under which new members may be admitted to the New Development Bank. Issued pursuant to the membership provisions of the 2014 Articles of Agreement. Governs subsequent expansions of NDB membership beyond the five founding shareholders.

dependencies.basis: The ESF is adopted under the powers of the Bank established by the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank and its Articles of Agreement; it operationalises the Bank’s mandate to finance infrastructure and sustainable development projects in a manner consistent with environmental and social sustainability.

The MoU situates cooperation within the institutional architecture created by the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank; the ICM members are the national development banks of the founding shareholders.

The MoU opens by recalling that NDB was established by the Governments of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa under the 2014 Agreement; BPIC itself is described as an outcome of a later BRICS Summit.
The MoU is a strategic cooperation instrument of the Bank created by the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement; signed in the presence of BRICS Leaders at the Xiamen Summit.
The MoU is concluded by the NDB (established under the 2014 Agreement) with the export credit agencies of the five founding members for the purpose of supporting NDB-financed projects.
The MoU is a cooperation instrument of the New Development Bank established by the 2014 Agreement; it targets infrastructure projects in NDB member countries, including Russia.

The Joint Statement records decisions on the Joint Statistical Publication work programme, congratulates the host on the JSP Snapshot, and sets the forward agenda for statistical cooperation that produces the annual JSP series.
The MoU explicitly recalls that NDB is a multilateral development bank established by the Governments of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa with the mandate set out in the 2014 Agreement.

The 2022 MoU between NDB and the ICM members builds on the earlier Framework Agreement on Financial Cooperation that established the Interbank Cooperation Mechanism among the national development banks of the founding BRICS members.

The MoU is concluded by the New Development Bank (established under the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement) and situates the partnership within NDB’s mandate to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development in BRICS and other EMDCs.

The Ufa Declaration explicitly welcomes the entry into force of the Agreement on the New Development Bank signed in Fortaleza and the inaugural meeting of the NDB Board of Governors held on the eve of the Summit.

The Declaration welcomes the conclusion of the ratification process of the Treaty Establishing a Contingent Reserve Arrangement and its entry into force, as well as the signing of the Inter-Central Bank Agreement that sets the technical parameters of CRA operations.
The Goa Declaration notes with satisfaction the operationalisation of the New Development Bank (created by the 2014 Agreement), the first set of loans, and progress on the Africa Regional Centre.

The Beijing Declaration congratulates NDB on its permanent headquarters and regional offices and welcomes decisions on admission of new members under the membership provisions of the Articles of Agreement annexed to the 2014 Agreement.
The Declaration supports amendments to the CRA Treaty and related documents to enhance flexibility and responsiveness, and notes progress on test runs of the CRA mechanism.

The official members list is maintained pursuant to Article 2 and the membership provisions of the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank (2014); it records both founding members and subsequent accessions under the 2017 Terms for Admission of New Members.

Egypt’s membership became effective upon deposit of the instrument of accession in accordance with the provisions of the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank (2014) and the Terms, Conditions and Procedures for the Admission of New Members (2017).
UAE membership became effective upon deposit of the instrument of accession under the membership provisions of the 2014 Articles of Agreement and the 2017 Terms for Admission of New Members.

The Local Currency Credit Line Master Agreement is one of the operational instruments developed under the Framework Agreement on Financial Cooperation that established the BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism in 2011; subsequent revisions continue to reference that framework.

The Multilateral Letter of Credit Confirmation Facility Agreement is a companion instrument signed under the same Interbank Cooperation Mechanism framework that produced the Local Currency Credit Line Master Agreement.
Algeria deposited its instrument of accession in accordance with the provisions of the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank (2014).

Successive Leaders’ Declarations, including the 2025 Rio de Janeiro Declaration issued under Brazilian chairmanship, continue to reaffirm the institutional architecture of the New Development Bank established by the 2014 Fortaleza instruments as a core pillar of BRICS economic-financial cooperation.

The Xiamen Declaration records satisfaction with the establishment of the New Development Bank (created by the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement) and welcomes the launch of the Africa Regional Centre, Project Preparation Fund, and permanent headquarters.

The Johannesburg Declaration welcomes the upcoming establishment of the Americas Regional Office and notes NDB Board of Governors discussions on the Bank’s future development, situating these under the institutional framework created in 2014.
The Declaration notes steps undertaken to strengthen operational readiness of the Contingent Reserve Arrangement and welcomes a successful test run of the de-linked portion of the CRA mechanism.

The Brasília Declaration explicitly marks the 5th anniversary of the signing of the NDB’s Articles of Agreement in Fortaleza and welcomes the opening of regional offices under the Bank’s constitutive framework.

The Moscow Declaration commends NDB COVID-19 emergency financing, welcomes the Eurasian Regional Centre, and supports the membership-expansion process conducted under the 2014 Agreement and subsequent Board of Governors decisions.

The New Delhi Declaration lists the creation of the New Development Bank among the major achievements of 15 years of BRICS cooperation and looks forward to the Bank’s second General Strategy and further institutional development under its constitutive instruments.

Decreto nº 8.624 is the formal Brazilian promulgation act whose sole purpose is to give domestic legal effect to the Agreement on the New Development Bank signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014; it records the congressional approval and the external entry-into-force date of 3 July 2015.

The Special Appropriation instrument records South Africa’s parliamentary ratification of the 2014 Agreement and appropriates the first capital instalment required under the Articles of Agreement after entry into force on 3 July 2015.

The Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress ratified the Agreement on the New Development Bank on 1 July 2015, enabling China to complete its domestic procedures and deposit the instrument that contributed to the Agreement’s entry into force on 3 July 2015.

The Procurement Policy is explicitly guided by Article 21 of the Agreement on the New Development Bank and is adopted pursuant to the purpose and functions of the Bank as stipulated in Articles 2 and 3 of that Agreement.

The Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership was adopted at the VII BRICS Summit in Ufa and is recorded in the Ufa Declaration as the key guideline for expanding trade, investment and financial cooperation among the member countries.

The Information Disclosure Policy is explicitly grounded in Article 15 of the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank, which requires the Bank to ensure transparency of its proceedings and to elaborate rules regarding access to its documents.

The Anti-Corruption, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money Laundering Policy is a core governance instrument of the Bank established by the 2014 Agreement; it applies to all NDB operations and projects financed under the Bank’s mandate.

The Code of Business Conduct and Ethics defines confidential information by reference to the categories set out in the Information Disclosure Policy and requires personnel to respect those classifications.

The Whistleblower Procedures are based on the principles and reporting obligations set out in the Anti-Corruption, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Money Laundering Policy and the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics.

The annual reports of the BRICS Business Council are produced under the cooperative relationship formalised by the 2017 MoU on Strategic Cooperation between the NDB and the BRICS Business Council; successive reports continue to address NDB financing and project facilitation.

The 2025 Annual Report explicitly recommends that governments request the New Development Bank (established under the 2014 Agreement) to create or expand specific financing lines and fast-track processes for infrastructure and low-carbon projects.

The MoU on Science, Technology and Innovation was prepared and referenced in the period of the Ufa Summit; the Ufa Declaration and related Russian Government documentation locate it within the broader BRICS cooperation agenda adopted at that summit.

The Evaluation Policy governs the independent evaluation function of the Bank created by the 2014 Agreement and provides the basis for the Independent Evaluation Office’s assessments of development results against the Bank’s strategies and mandate.
The technical meetings of BRICS NSOs are the standing preparatory mechanism that sets data requirements, chapter structure and timelines for each annual edition of the Joint Statistical Publication.

The 2024 edition is one annual issue of the continuous Joint Statistical Publication series; it is compiled from national data supplied by the member NSOs under the same cooperative framework that produces every year’s JSP.
The Independent Evaluation Office’s Development Results reports are produced under the framework and standards set by the NDB Evaluation Policy.

The Rules of Procedure of the Board of Governors are adopted under the authority of, and are intended to be complementary to, the Agreement on the New Development Bank and the annexed Articles of Agreement; in the event of conflict the Agreement and Articles prevail.

The Rules of Procedure of the Board of Directors are adopted under the authority of the Agreement on the New Development Bank and the annexed Articles of Agreement and shall be construed accordingly; the Agreement and Articles prevail in case of conflict.

The Board of Directors Governance Structure document locates the Board’s responsibilities under the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank and describes the committee architecture established to support those responsibilities.
The Policy explicitly covers NDB sovereign loans and loans with sovereign guarantee as allowed under Articles 18 and 19 of the Agreement on the New Development Bank.

The Policy is grounded in Article 21 (sound banking principles, economy and efficiency) and Article 13e (decisions based only on economic considerations) of the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank.
The Policy is grounded in Article 1 of the Articles of Agreement, which provides that the Bank shall cooperate with international organisations and other financial entities.

The Action Plan is adopted under the BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation cooperation framework and builds on the 2015 MoU on Cooperation in the Fields of Science, Technology and Innovation among the Governments of the BRICS States.

The Roadmap builds on the 2015 Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership, which identified the services sector as a priority area for collaboration, and on the subsequent Framework for Cooperation on Trade in Services.
The Implementation Roadmap is explicitly devised for the trade and investment related aspects of the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2025.

The Joint Statement addresses the development of the New Development Bank and supports building the NDB into a new type of multilateral development institution, situating it within the institutional architecture established by the 2014 Agreement.

The Joint Statement continues the annual Heads of NSOs series that sets the work programme and priorities for the Joint Statistical Publication and related statistical cooperation, including digital dissemination and SNA 2025 transition.
The 2025 Snapshot is one annual issue of the continuous shorter companion series to the full Joint Statistical Publication, drawing selected key indicators from the main JSP.
The Technical Assistance Policy is a Board-approved operational policy of the Bank established by the 2014 Agreement and supports project preparation and capacity building under the Bank’s mandate.

The Policy on Guarantees forms part of the suite of financial-instrument policies that operationalise the Bank’s ability, under the Articles of Agreement, to support projects through loans, guarantees, equity participation and other instruments.

The Strategic Framework of BRICS Customs Cooperation was developed under the trade-facilitation agenda set out in the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership and subsequent Trade Ministers’ work programmes.

Every NDB Annual Report opens by locating the Bank’s legal existence in the 15 July 2014 Agreement signed by the five founding members and the annexed Articles of Agreement that entered into force on 3 July 2015. The 2024 Report and prior editions treat the Agreement as the constitutive instrument.

The Strategy is adopted by the Board of Governors under the powers conferred by the Articles of Agreement annexed to the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement; subsequent Annual Reports explicitly locate strategy cycles under that constitutive instrument.

Official description states the Snapshot is a shortened version of the full Joint Statistical Publication, selecting key comparable indicators from the main JSP for wider dissemination. Issued annually alongside the full edition since 2021.

The JSP work programme, chapter structure, data requirements, and host rotation are set and confirmed at the annual meeting of Heads of NSOs; the Joint Statement records those decisions and the presentation of the year’s JSP at the Leaders’ Summit.

The host agreement text explicitly takes into account the Agreement on the New Development Bank together with the Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank contained in the Annex to that Agreement, concluded among the five founding governments. The Centre is established as a regional office of the Bank created by the 2014 instrument.

The Federal Law is the formal Russian ratification act whose sole purpose is to approve and bring into force the 13 November 2019 host agreement. Entry into force of the international agreement (7 December 2020) is conditional on this domestic ratification.

Federal Law 29-FZ is the Russian ratification statute for the Fortaleza Agreement on the New Development Bank. Deposit of Russia’s instrument of acceptance under this law was a necessary condition for the 2014 Agreement’s entry into force on 3 July 2015.

Article 6 of the 2014 CRA Treaty mandates that the five founding central banks ‘shall enter into an inter-central bank agreement setting out the required operational procedures and guidelines’ in order to carry out the liquidity and precautionary instruments. The inter-central-bank agreement is therefore the operational implementation layer required by the Treaty itself.

The 2022–2026 Strategy is the successor cycle to the first General Strategy 2017–2021; Annual Reports and strategy documents locate the later cycle as building directly on the experience and framework of the initial strategy period.

Leaders’ declarations under successive presidencies, including the 2024 Kazan Declaration issued under Russian chairmanship, reaffirm support for the New Development Bank and the institutional architecture created by the 2014 Fortaleza instruments as part of the BRICS economic-financial pillar.

Preamble of the South Africa host agreement explicitly takes into account the Agreement on the New Development Bank and its Annex (Articles of Agreement) and recalls Article 4 of the Articles of Agreement stipulating that the first regional office of the NDB shall be in Johannesburg.

The headquarters agreement is concluded under the powers conferred by the 2014 Agreement and Articles of Agreement; NDB lists it among core documents that operationalise the Bank’s seat established by the constitutive instrument.

Host agreements for regional offices are concluded pursuant to the Articles of Agreement annexed to the 2014 Fortaleza Agreement, which authorise the Bank to establish offices necessary for the performance of its functions.
Same constitutive basis as other regional-office host agreements: Articles of Agreement of the New Development Bank (2014) authorise establishment of offices necessary for the Bank’s functions.

Paragraphs of the Fortaleza Declaration announce the signing of the Agreement on the New Development Bank, record the initial authorised and subscribed capital, and name the first chairs of the Board of Governors and Board of Directors. The Declaration is the contemporaneous political instrument that frames the treaty signing.

The Declaration explicitly announces the signing of the Treaty for the establishment of the BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement with an initial size of USD 100 billion and describes its precautionary purpose.

The IEO Report evaluates projects against alignment with NDB general strategies (including the 2022–2026 cycle) as well as national priorities and the SDGs. Strategy alignment is an explicit evaluation criterion.

The synthesis draws on project portfolio data, approval and disbursement figures, and results indicators that are also reported in successive NDB Annual Reports; the IEO report states it covers projects representing ~56% of total disbursed financing as of the cut-off date.

The Terms, Conditions and Procedures document is issued under the membership provisions of the Articles of Agreement annexed to the 2014 Agreement on the New Development Bank; it operationalises the admission rules set out in the constitutive instrument.

Successive Leaders’ Declarations, including Johannesburg II 2023, reaffirm support for the New Development Bank as a core pillar of the BRICS economic-financial architecture established by the 2014 Fortaleza instruments.

_dropped.edge: CRA Governing Council Procedural Rules and Standing Committee Procedural Rules (full standalone public text)
_dropped.why: Bank of Russia confirmed that the Governing Council approved Procedural Rules for both the Governing Council and the Standing Committee at the inaugural meetings in Ankara on 4 September 2015. These rules are required by the 2014 CRA Treaty. However, a freely downloadable, permanently titled public PDF equivalent to the Treaty or the NDB host agreements was not located on official portals in this pass. Existence is documented; full text recovery deferred.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia-linked MoU or institutional instrument within the confirmed BRICS set
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Per standing instruction, Saudi Arabia is excluded from the confirmed full-member set. Any instruments involving Saudi entities are dropped with reason 'Saudi'.

_dropped.edge: individual NDB project appraisal or loan agreements as separate nodes in this batch
_dropped.why: Numerous project-level documents exist and are high-quality. They are better treated in later densification once country-level domestic series (especially Russia) are in place, so that evidence-grade edges to national statistics or sectoral reports can be drawn.

_dropped.edge: full public text of the 2011 BRICS Interbank Cooperation Mechanism Framework Agreement as a standalone permanent PDF
_dropped.why: Existence and subsequent revisions are confirmed by multiple official sources (including DBSA and NDB references). A clean, permanently hosted public PDF of the original 2011 text was not located in this pass; the node is retained on the strength of secondary official descriptions and the later NDB–ICM MoU that builds on it.

_dropped.edge: Iran formal NDB membership / instrument of accession
_dropped.why: Iran is a full BRICS member (joined 2024). However, as of the latest official NDB members list, Iran does not appear among confirmed NDB members. Central-bank statements indicate intent to join, but no instrument of accession or Board of Governors admission decision with public effective date was located. Deferred until a titled public document appears.

_dropped.edge: Ethiopia formal NDB membership / instrument of accession
_dropped.why: Ethiopia is a full BRICS member and has been approved as a prospective NDB member by the Board of Governors. Domestic ratification processes were reported as underway in mid-2026, but deposit of the instrument of accession and formal membership effective date had not yet been published on the official NDB members list at the time of this batch. Track for a later pass.

_dropped.edge: Indonesia formal NDB membership / instrument of accession
_dropped.why: Indonesia is a full BRICS member (joined 2025). No confirmed NDB membership or instrument of accession appears on the official NDB members list or in contemporary NDB announcements examined for this batch.

_dropped.edge: full public text of the revised 2024 ICM Local Currency Credit Line Agreement as a standalone permanent PDF
_dropped.why: Official secondary sources (DBSA, national treasuries) confirm that a 2024 revision of the local-currency credit-line framework was signed to accommodate new members. A clean, permanently hosted public PDF of the revised text was not located; the node is retained on the strength of the official descriptions and the earlier Master Agreement lineage.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia NDB accession or related instrument
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Per standing instruction, Saudi Arabia remains excluded from the confirmed full-member set. No Saudi NDB membership appears on the official list.

_dropped.edge: India domestic ratification instrument for the 2014 NDB Agreement as a clean standalone public Act/Decree
_dropped.why: India completed the necessary domestic procedures that allowed the 2014 Agreement to enter into force on 3 July 2015. However, a single, easily citable, permanently titled public Act or Gazette notification equivalent to Brazil’s Decreto 8.624 or the Russian Federal Laws was not located in this pass. Secondary sources confirm ratification occurred; full primary text recovery deferred.

_dropped.edge: full public text of the NDB Project Preparation Facility operational guidelines as a standalone titled policy document
_dropped.why: Multiple Leaders’ Declarations (Xiamen 2017, Brasília 2019) reference the establishment and first projects of the Project Preparation Facility. A dedicated, permanently hosted public policy document setting out its rules was not located in the same form as the ESF or Procurement Policy.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia-related declaration language or accession instrument
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Per standing instruction.

_dropped.edge: earlier individual BRICS Business Council Annual Reports (pre-2025) as separate full nodes
_dropped.why: Multiple prior annual reports exist (including the 2023/24 Russian presidency edition). They can be added as year-specific instances under the recurring series node in a later densification pass if needed; the 2025 edition is captured as the current high-visibility instance.

_dropped.edge: full public text of the 2015 BRICS STI MoU as a clean English-language permanent PDF
_dropped.why: A Russian Government order of 14 March 2015 attaches the draft MoU text. A clean, multi-language permanent public PDF equivalent to the NDB host agreements was not located; the node is retained on the strength of the official order and secondary references.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia chapter or recommendation inside Business Council reports
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Per standing instruction.

_dropped.edge: full public standalone text of every minor NDB operational guideline listed in internal policy inventories (Country Partnership Plan details, private-placement procedures, etc.)
_dropped.why: NDB maintains an extensive internal inventory of Board-approved policies. The highest-centrality public policy documents (ESF, Procurement, Information Disclosure, Anti-Corruption, Sovereign Loans, Financial Management, Guarantees, Technical Assistance, Evaluation, Board Rules) have been captured. Remaining lower-visibility guidelines can be added in later passes if specific evidence-grade edges are needed.

_dropped.edge: BRICS Pay / BRICS Bridge / BCBPI as fully operational titled public instruments with permanent downloadable texts
_dropped.why: Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors statements and secondary sources describe the BRICS Cross-Border Payments Initiative (BCBPI), BRICS Bridge concepts, and related payment-system work. These remain largely conceptual / voluntary / non-binding or at pilot stage; no single constitutive public treaty or fully operational permanent instrument equivalent to the CRA Treaty or NDB Agreement was located.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia-linked instrument or chapter
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Per standing instruction.

_dropped.edge: any Saudi Arabia participation in JSP / NDB / CRA / host agreements / declarations
_dropped.why: [original reason tag: Saudi] Saudi Arabia was invited at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit but has not completed formal accession. Saudi Economy Minister statements confirm the Kingdom is still assessing membership. NDB membership list does not include Saudi Arabia. Per explicit instruction, all Saudi material is dropped with reason 'Saudi'.

_dropped.edge: ndb-annual-report -> brics-cra-treaty-2014
_dropped.why: While both instruments were signed the same day in Fortaleza and are frequently discussed together in secondary literature, the NDB Annual Reports examined do not contain an explicit methodological or data citation of the CRA Treaty. CRA is a separate central-bank liquidity arrangement, not an NDB instrument.

_dropped.edge: brics-jsp -> individual national series (Rosstat national accounts, CPI, etc.)
_dropped.why: The JSP explicitly compiles and publishes national series supplied by each member NSO (including Rosstat). Concrete edges to specific domestic series will be added once the corresponding national batches exist.

_dropped.edge: institutional identity nodes for 'BRICS' or 'NDB' as organisations
_dropped.why: DATA SPEC forbids institutional-identity nodes. Only titled published documents (treaties, annual reports, joint publications, joint statements, host agreements, declarations) qualify.

_dropped.edge: full public text of CRA Inter-Central Bank Agreement as a freely downloadable standalone PDF
_dropped.why: Article 6 of the Treaty requires the inter-central-bank agreement, and its existence and function are clear. However, the complete operational text is not published in the same open, permanent form as the Treaty itself on the major public portals examined. Node retained because the Treaty’s own language establishes its necessity; full text recovery deferred.

_dropped.edge: Kazan Declaration direct data dependency on JSP or NDB Annual Report
_dropped.why: The Declaration is a high-level political statement. While it references the institutional architecture, it does not contain explicit methodological or data-use claims that would support a calculated_from / uses_data_from edge to the statistical or annual-report series.

_dropped.edge: project-level individual evaluation reports as separate nodes
_dropped.why: Individual project performance evaluation reports exist and are high-quality. They are better treated in a later densification pass once country-level domestic series are in place, so that edges to national statistics can be drawn with evidence.

_dropped.edge: CRA Standing Committee procedural rules as a standalone published titled document
_dropped.why: The 2014 Treaty authorises the Standing Committee to prepare its own procedural rules, but a freely available, permanently titled public document equivalent to the Treaty or the host agreements was not located.

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.
